songInfo.album: Mellon Collie and the Infinite Sadness
songInfo.tuning: Half-Step Down (Eb Ab Db Gb Bb Eb)

scalesUsed.notes: E - F# - G# - A - B - C# - D# - E
scalesUsed.application: Underpins Billy Corgan's nostalgic octave melody and open-drone E major / Asus2 verse progression (sounding in Eb major due to half-step-down tuning)

scalesUsed.notes: C# - D# - E - F# - G# - A - B - C#
scalesUsed.application: Drives the wistful F#m11 - B - E - C#m chorus progression and bridge octave shifts

keyAndScale.modalCharacter: Wistful, coming-of-age E Ionian / Lydian dream-rock built on sliding octave shapes and ringing open B and high E drone strings
keyAndScale.keySignature: 4 sharps (F#, C#, G#, D# in fretboard shapes; sounds in Eb major)
keyAndScale.relativeMinor: C# minor is the relative minor of E major

mainProgression.progression: Imaj7 - IVsus2 (Verse) | ii11 - Vadd11 - I - vi7 (Chorus)
mainProgression.progressionDescription: Alternates between a two-chord hypnotic verse loop (Emaj7 to Asus2 with sliding A-and-G-string octaves) and a sweeping chorus progression that keeps the top two strings open throughout.
mainProgression.description: Alternates between a two-chord hypnotic verse loop (Emaj7 to Asus2 with sliding A-and-G-string octaves) and a sweeping chorus progression that keeps the top two strings open throughout.

sectionProgressions.description: 6th-fret D# octave on the A and G strings resolving to an open Asus2 chord followed by a fast descending octave run (11-9-7-6-4-2)
Lush open-drone barre chords climbing up the neck while the B and high E strings shimmer continuously

sectionProgressions.section: Bridge ('The street heats the urgency of now')
sectionProgressions.description: Borrowed flat-six (C5/G) power chord twist before returning to the main octave groove
E major A-and-G-string octave sliding exercise across the fretboard

harmonicFunction: Emaj7 (Imaj7) - Nostalgic major seventh tonic established by the low E bass and D# octave
Asus2 (IVsus2) - Open, airy subdominant chord that anchors the rapid descending octave run
F#m11 & Badd11 (ii - V) - Open-string extended chords creating a dreamy pre-chorus/chorus lift
C#m7 (vi7) - Relative minor chord grounding the end of each chorus line

techniques.name: A-and-G-String Octave Sliding & Open Drone Chords
techniques.description: Fretting octave shapes on the 5th (A) and 3rd (G) strings while muting the middle D string and sliding rapidly down the E major scale degrees (frets 11-9-7-6-4-2)

notes: D# Octave (over E): 0-6-X-8-0-0
Octave Run: 11/13 → 9/11 → 7/9 → 6/8 → 4/6 → 2/4 on A/G strings
sequence: Strum the low E string with the 6th/8th fret D# octave shape on the A and G strings
Switch to open Asus2 (X-0-2-2-0-0) for the first half of the second bar
Execute the signature descending octave slide on the A and G strings: 11 → 9 → 7 → 6 → 4 → 2
Keep your index finger slightly flattened to mute the D string throughout the octave run
tips: Maintain a fixed two-fret spacing between your index finger (A string) and ring/pinky finger (G string) as you slide down the neck
Look ahead to your target fret (fret 2) rather than watching your fingers during the fast octave slide
In the chorus, let the open B and high E strings ring out on F#m11 (2-4-4-2-0-0), Badd11 (X-2-4-4-0-0), and C#m7 (X-4-6-6-0-0)
details.progression: Emaj7 - Asus2 | F#m11 - Badd11 - E - C#m7

techniques.name: Open-String Extended Chord Voicings & Propulsive 127 BPM Strumming
techniques.description: Voicing shimmering extended chords (F#m11, Badd11, C#m7) while maintaining continuous 127 BPM eighth-note rhythm with ringing open B and high E drone strings

notes: F#m11: 2-4-4-2-0-0 (thumb or index on fret 2, open top strings)
Badd11: X-2-4-4-0-0 (movable shape with open high strings)
C#m7: X-4-6-6-0-0 (dreamy modern rock minor voicing)
sequence: Fret the F#m11 shape cleanly without deadening strings 1 and 2
Slide up to Badd11, keeping the high drone strings vibrating
Hit the open E major chord and resolve to C#m7
Maintain relaxed pendulum motion in the strumming wrist at 127 BPM
tips: Keep your fingers arched over strings 1 and 2 to avoid accidental damping
Use a 0.73mm pick for crisp string separation without harsh pick slap
Let the acoustic-electric textures blend to recreate Flood and Alan Moulder's layered production
details.progression: F#m11 - Badd11 - E - C#m7 Chorus Cycle

sections.name: Intro Octave Riff & Drum Machine Loop
sections.description: Billy Corgan's unmistakable opening statement with D# octaves over the open E bass and drum machine pulse.
notes: Mute the 4th (D) string cleanly with the underside of your index finger
Let the open low E string drone under the 6th/8th fret D# octave
Slide smoothly down 11-9-7-6-4-2 on beats 3 and 4 of bar 2

sections.name: Verse 1 Emaj7 - Asus2 Octave Glide
sections.description: The hypnotic verse groove accompanying Corgan's nostalgic lyrics ('Shakedown 1979, cool kids never have the time').
notes: Lock into the steady 127 BPM tempo
Keep the two-fret hand frame locked as you slide down
Open Asus2 provides a gentle harmonic release

sections.name: Chorus 1 Dreamy Open Drones ('Shakedown 1979')
sections.description: Dreamy chorus progression moving from F#m11 and Badd11 up to E and C#m7.
notes: Keep strings 1 and 2 open on every chord for a unified shoegaze shimmer
Strum with a steady, propulsive eighth-note feel at 127 BPM
Emphasize the bass root transitions cleanly

sections.name: Verse 2 Melodic Octave Run & Vocal Accents
sections.description: Verse 2 continues the driving groove with vocal ad-libs and subtle dynamic lifts.
notes: Maintain clean palm contact only where damping is needed
Ensure the high E string rings out during the Emaj7 chord
Crisp transition on the rapid octave slide

sections.name: Bridge Flat-VI Power Chord Shift
sections.description: Unexpected bridge shift to borrowed C5 flat-six power chord ('The street heats the urgency of now').
notes: Heavier pick attack on the power chords
Hit the C5 chord on fret 3 of the A string with authority
Build the crescendo into the final chorus

sections.name: Outro Hypnotic Octave Fade
sections.description: The iconic main octave riff ascends and descends over the fading drum loop and vocal echoes.
notes: Maintain steady, relaxed wrist motion
Let the octave notes sing out without fret buzz
Gradually soften dynamics as the song fades

guitar.recommended: Fender Stratocaster (with Lace Sensor pickups) or Fender Jazzmaster
guitar.pickup: Neck + Middle single-coil position for glassy verse chime; Bridge pickup for chorus drive

amp.recommended: Marshall JMP-1 Preamp into Mesa/Boogie Strategy 500 Power Amp

effects.distortion: Light tube overdrive or Electro-Harmonix Big Muff Pi (rolled back for bridge thickness)
effects.other: Optical compressor for even octave sustain

beginner.title: Octave Shape & Open Asus2
steps: Form the 6th-fret A / 8th-fret G octave shape and practice muting the middle D string
Practice switching from the Emaj7 octave shape to the open Asus2 chord (X-0-2-2-0-0)
Learn the open-drone chorus chords: F#m11, Badd11, E, and C#m7

intermediate.title: The Descending Octave Run
steps: Master the descending octave slide (11 → 9 → 7 → 6 → 4 → 2) slowly at 90 BPM
Connect the Asus2 chord directly into the octave run without pausing on beat 3
Play the verse and chorus seamlessly at 127 BPM

advanced.title: Bridge Modulation & Full Studio Precision
steps: Execute the bridge modulation (E5 - C5 - A5 - B5) and octave melodies
Maintain flawless D-string muting even while strumming aggressively at full tempo
Layer the rhythm and octave parts with a looper pedal

commonMistakes: Letting the open D string ring out inside the octave shapes, creating a muddy cluster
Changing the distance between the index and ring fingers while sliding down from fret 11 to fret 2
Starting the descending octave run too late and missing beat 1 of the next Emaj7 bar
practiceRoutine: 5 minutes: Isolated octave shape D-string muting check across frets 2, 4, 6, 7, 9, and 11
5 minutes: Descending octave slide (11-9-7-6-4-2) looped with a metronome at 100 BPM → 127 BPM
5 minutes: Chorus open-drone chord transitions (F#m11 → Badd11 → E → C#m7)
focusAreas: Clean index-finger muting of the 4th string
Ringing open B and high E strings during the chorus
metronomeWork: Start at 95 BPM to ensure every octave position in the descending run is articulated clearly
Gradually increase to 127 BPM while keeping the strumming hand relaxed
Lock the Emaj7 downbeat directly to click 1 after the slide
